definition.text: In an economic model, an exogenous variable has its value set outside the model, while an endogenous variable's value is determined by the model.

facts.text: In econometrics, an endogenous random variable is correlated with the error term, while an exogenous variable is not; this is related to but distinct from the modelling sense.
A variable can be exogenous in one model and endogenous in another, for example when one model is a component of a broader model.
The IS model treats the interest rate as exogenous and output as endogenous; the LM model takes income as given and determines the interest rate; combined in IS-LM, both are endogenous.
Comparative statics compares outcomes before and after a change in an exogenous parameter, using derivatives to see how each endogenous variable moves.
